language.title: Language
language.description: The language of the interface. It follows your account to other browsers.
language.label: Interface language

toast.changedDescription: Other browsers signed in to this account were signed out.

password.title: Change password
password.description: Your other sessions are signed out; this one stays signed in.

settingsFile.title: Settings file
settingsFile.description: The settings on these pages are saved in one file on the server. If a change keeps Athena from starting or locks you out, fix it there in any text editor, then restart Athena.
settingsFile.loadFailed: Couldn't load where the file is: {{error}}
settingsFile.help: athena config check on the server shows what's wrong with it, with line numbers. The version before the last save is kept next to it as athena.json.bak.

system.title: System
system.description: Switches that apply to everyone on this server. Changes are written to the audit log.

terminal.label: Web terminal
terminal.description: A shell on this server and in containers, from the browser. Turning it off also closes open sessions.

updateCheck.label: Update notice
updateCheck.description: Once a day, ask GitHub for the latest Athena release and show a notice when a newer one is out. Nothing is sent but the request itself: no version, host name or settings.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: Athena checks for a new release once a day (the switch above). Updating restarts Athena; your apps keep running.

localAi.running_one: {{list}} is running on this server. Its models run on your own hardware and nothing leaves the server.
localAi.running_other: {{list}} are running on this server. Their models run on your own hardware and nothing leaves the server.
localAi.usePort: Use the AI server on port {{port}}

webdav.title: Network share (WebDAV)
webdav.description: Open the file manager's locations as a drive in Finder, Windows Explorer or a Linux file manager.
webdav.label: WebDAV
webdav.help: Off by default. Anyone with the WebDAV password can read and change every location.

passwordHint.copyNow: Copy it now: it isn't shown again.
passwordHint.set: A password is set. Making a new one signs out every device using the old one.
passwordHint.none: Make a password to sign in. It's separate from your Athena password.

plainHttp.title: Not encrypted
plainHttp.description: Athena is open over plain HTTP, so the WebDAV password and files cross the network unencrypted. Use it on a network you trust, or put Athena behind HTTPS.

howto.macos: macOS: Finder → Go → Connect to Server, then the address.
howto.windows: Windows: File Explorer → This PC → Map network drive, then the address. Over plain HTTP Windows only signs in after setting BasicAuthLevel to 2 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WebClient\Parameters and restarting the WebClient service.
howto.linux: Linux: in Files (GNOME) or Dolphin, connect to {{url}}.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: Changes apply right away and follow your account to other browsers.

type.title: Typography and shape
type.styleSoon: switching styles is coming in a later version

preset.title: Preset code
preset.description: A shadcn preset code captures these settings in a few characters.
preset.use: Use it with npx shadcn init --preset {{code}}, or share it.
preset.invalid: That isn't a shadcn preset code.
preset.ignored: Athena can't apply {{parts}} yet, so those parts were skipped.
preset.fill: Fills in the colors, fonts and radius from a code made on <link>ui.shadcn.com/create</link>.

tunnel.secretSaved: Saved. Type a new value to replace it

cloudflare.quickHelp: A random trycloudflare.com address that needs no account. It changes every time the tunnel starts.
cloudflare.apiTokenPlaceholder: A Cloudflare API token with Tunnel permissions
cloudflare.tunnelNameHelp: The named tunnel in your Cloudflare account.
cloudflare.domainHelp: Needs a DNS record pointing at the tunnel.

tailscale.help: Set with tailscale up on this server.

ngrok.freeDescription: One tunnel, 40 connections a minute, and a new random address each session.

autoStart.label: Start on boot
autoStart.off: Remote access no longer starts on boot
autoStart.help: Installs a system service that starts the tunnel with the server.

tunnel.title: Remote access
tunnel.description: Reach Athena from anywhere through Cloudflare, Tailscale or ngrok, without opening ports on your router.
tunnel.label: Remote access
tunnel.help: Anyone with the address reaches your sign-in page, so use a strong password.

exposed.title: Reachable from the internet
exposed.description: While this is on, the web terminal, package installs and the AI assistant are one password away from anyone who finds the address. Turn off <terminal>the terminal</terminal> or the <assistant>assistant</assistant> if you don't need them remotely.

port.label: Local port
port.help: The port Athena listens on, which the tunnel forwards to.

unavailable.title: HTTPS isn't available
unavailable.description: This Athena server doesn't report HTTPS support.

status.encryptedLetsEncrypt: Athena encrypts the connection with a certificate from Let's Encrypt. Plain HTTP stays on port {{port}}.
status.encryptedCustom: Athena encrypts the connection with your custom certificate. Plain HTTP stays on port {{port}}.
status.encryptedSelf: Athena encrypts the connection with its own certificate. Plain HTTP stays on port {{port}}.
status.plain: Athena is served over plain HTTP on port {{port}}, so passwords and files cross the network unencrypted.
status.renewalStillServed: The current certificate is still served until it expires.

https.certificateReadyHint: Save with Let's Encrypt selected to start serving it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Changes apply right away; Athena doesn't restart.

mode.label: Mode
mode.selfHelp: Athena makes its own certificate authority (CA). Trust it once on each device and browsers show a padlock with no warning. Works on your home network with no domain.
mode.letsencryptHelp: A free certificate every browser trusts, for a domain you own that points at this server. Renewed automatically.
mode.customHelp: Upload your own certificate and private key (PEM format). Athena serves them as-is; no automatic renewal.

port.label: HTTPS port
port.help: Ports below 1024 (like 443) may need Athena to run as root. You may have to allow the port in the host's firewall.
port.taken: Port {{port}} is Athena's HTTP port. Pick another one.

redirect.label: Send browsers to HTTPS
redirect.help: Pages opened on port {{port}} move to HTTPS. File shares, webhooks, apps and the server itself keep using plain HTTP.

names.label: Extra names
names.help: The certificate already covers this server's name, its .local name and its network addresses. Add any other name or address you open Athena with, separated by commas.

https.lockedOut: Locked out? Run {{command}} on the server and restart Athena.

confirm.title: Send browsers to HTTPS?
confirm.redirect: After saving, opening Athena on port {{port}} takes you to <url>{{url}}</url>.
confirm.letsencrypt: Open Athena by its domain name there; other names get a certificate warning.
confirm.custom: Your custom certificate is served; browsers trust it if it's from a known CA.
confirm.self: Until you trust Athena's CA on a device, its browser shows a warning there.
confirm.recovery: If you can't get back in, run <cmd>{{command}}</cmd> on the server and restart Athena.

le.domainsHelp: Separate several with commas. Each must point at this server in public DNS. A wildcard (*.example.com) needs the DNS challenge.
le.emailHelp: Let's Encrypt writes here if a certificate is about to expire.
le.httpHelp: Let's Encrypt connects to port 80 on this server, so it must be reachable from the internet (forward it on your router).
le.dnsHelp: Athena adds a temporary DNS record through your DNS provider. No open ports; works for wildcards.
le.port80Title: Port 80 can't be opened right now
le.port80Description: Another program uses it, or Athena isn't allowed to open it. Free port 80 or use the DNS challenge.
le.stagingHelp: For trying things out: browsers don't trust its certificates, but its limits are generous.
le.getThenSave: Get a certificate, then save to start serving it.

custom.certHelp: Paste the full PEM-encoded certificate or certificate chain.
custom.keyHelp: Paste the PEM-encoded private key. It will be stored encrypted.

trust.title: Trust Athena on your devices
trust.description: Install Athena's CA once on each phone, tablet and computer you use. Then the browser trusts every certificate Athena makes, including renewals.
trust.fingerprintHelp: Check it matches what the device shows before trusting the file.
trust.rotatedHint: Download it and trust it again on each device.
trust.rotateHint: Make a new CA if the key may have leaked. Every device has to trust the new one.
trust.confirmDescription: Devices that trust the current CA show a warning until you install the new one on each of them.

macos.label: macOS
macos.step1: Open the downloaded file. Keychain Access adds it to the login keychain.
macos.step2: In Keychain Access, double-click Athena Local CA, open Trust, and set When using this certificate to Always Trust.
macos.step3: Close the window and enter your Mac password. Restart the browser.

windows.label: Windows
windows.step1: Open the downloaded file and choose Install Certificate.
windows.step2: Pick Current User, then Place all certificates in the following store → Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
windows.step3: Finish and confirm the security warning. Restart the browser.

linux.label: Linux
linux.step3: Firefox and Chrome keep their own list on Linux: import the file under the browser's certificate settings, in Authorities.

ios.label: iPhone and iPad
ios.step1: Download the file in Safari and allow the profile download.
ios.step2: In Settings, open Profile Downloaded (or General → VPN & Device Management) and install it.
ios.step3: Go to General → About → Certificate Trust Settings and turn on full trust for Athena Local CA.

android.label: Android
android.step2: In Settings, search for CA certificate (usually Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate) and pick the file.
android.step3: Confirm the warning. Some apps ignore user certificates; browsers use them.
